papers.title: HIT-MAP: A scalable approach to multimodal mapping of subcellular organization.
papers.abstract: Multimodal mapping of subcellular protein organization through imaging and interaction proteomics has been mostly confined to large consortia, owing to high per-target costs, reliance on target-specific antibodies or libraries of epitope-tagged cDNAs, and the lack of unified pipelines for coordinated data acquisition. Here, we present HIT-MAP (high-throughput integrated tagging for cell mapping), an end-to-end framework that couples endogenous epitope tagging with optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging and affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS). Applied to a pilot set of 16 r
papers.summary: HIT-MAP is an end-to-end framework that combines endogenous epitope tagging, optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging, and affinity purification-mass spectrometry to map subcellular protein organization in a coordinated way. It aims to make multimodal subcellular mapping feasible for individual labs rather than only large consortia, demonstrated on a pilot set of 16 targets.

papers.title: Defining the Genetic and Phenotypic Landscape of Primary Immune Regulatory Disorders Using the ClinGen Validation Framework.
papers.abstract: Primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRDs) represent a rapidly growing group of inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) characterized by infection susceptibility, autoimmunity, inflammation, and lymphoproliferation. However, the core features of the gene-disease relationships underlying these conditions are often obscured by limitations in available published data. The Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) is an international collaborative effort that seeks to address this challenge for PIRDs and other monogenic diseases through a standardized framework for classifying the strength of gene-disease rela
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint applies the ClinGen gene-disease validity framework to systematically classify the strength of evidence linking genes to primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRDs), a growing subset of inborn errors of immunity. By standardizing how published data are evaluated, the work aims to clarify which gene-disease relationships are well-supported versus uncertain, providing a curated landscape of genetic and phenotypic features for these conditions.

papers.title: The CFDE Workbench: Integrating Metadata and Processed Data from Common Fund Programs.
papers.abstract: The NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) program was established to facilitate data accessibility and interoperability across multiple Common Fund (CF) programs, promote collaborations and accelerate discoveries by combining diverse data types from different CF programs. The CFDE Data Resource Center (DRC) was tasked with developing two web-based portals: an Information Portal to serve information about the CFDE, and a Data Portal to host harmonized metadata and processed data contributed by participating CF Data Coordination Centers (DCCs) and other sources. To achieve these goals, the CFDE
papers.summary: The CFDE Workbench is a web-based platform that integrates harmonized metadata and processed data from multiple NIH Common Fund programs, aiming to improve data accessibility and interoperability across diverse biomedical datasets. It provides an Information Portal and a Data Portal to enable cross-program data discovery and collaboration.

papers.title: PDBe-KB Complexes: Enabling Functional Insight from Macromolecular Complexes in the PDB.
papers.abstract: PDBe-KB Complexes is a set of webpages that aggregate experimentally determined macromolecular assemblies into unique complex-level records within the Protein Data Bank in Europe Knowledge Base framework. Each unique complex identifier unifies equivalent biological assemblies from the PDB that represent the same macromolecular complex, consolidating information on component identity, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and PISA-derived assembly properties within a consistent framework. Relationships between complexes are established by comparing their compositions, capturing both subcomplexes th
papers.summary: PDBe-KB Complexes is a new resource that groups equivalent macromolecular assemblies from the PDB into unified complex-level records, consolidating data on component identity, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and PISA-derived assembly properties. It also links related complexes by comparing their compositions to capture subcomplex relationships. This provides a consistent framework for gaining functional insight into macromolecular complexes.

papers.title: Utilization of advanced machine learning based on financial ontology induction for adaptive multilingual method in document recognition.
papers.abstract: A noise-robust framework is introduced for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction, designed to address the challenges posed by noisy and partially labeled multilingual financial documents. The method employs a confidence-based filtering mechanism to eliminate low-quality cross-lingual text pairs, followed by multi-view distillation to harmonize linguistic and structural representations of financial entities. An uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective further aligns entities across languages while reducing the influence of unreliable alignments. The resulting ontolo
papers.summary: This paper presents a semi-supervised machine learning framework for inducing financial ontologies across multiple languages from noisy, partially labeled documents. It uses confidence-based filtering, multi-view distillation, and uncertainty-aware contrastive learning to align financial entities across languages despite unreliable data. The result is a more noise-robust multilingual ontology induction method.

papers.title: Rabies Virus Glycoprotein G Variation Is Associated with Neurovirulence and Reduced Vamp2 Abundance in a Mouse Model of Direct CNS Infection.
papers.abstract: Rabies virus causes fatal neurological disease, but the mechanisms by which its glycoprotein G influences neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. In this study, we rescued two recombinant RABV LBNSE strains carrying G proteins from either the attenuated SAD-B19 strain or the virulent CVS11 strain, designated as rLBNSE-SfG and rLBNSE-CfG, respectively. Infection of primary mouse neurons and challenge experiments in mice showed that rLBNSE-CfG was associated with increased early neuronal infectivity and greater neurovirulence after intracerebral (i.c.) injection. Western blot analys
papers.summary: Researchers engineered two recombinant rabies viruses differing only in their glycoprotein G, derived from either an attenuated or virulent strain, and found that the virulent G variant increased early neuronal infectivity and neurovirulence after direct brain injection in mice. This virulence was linked to reduced abundance of the synaptic protein Vamp2, suggesting a mechanism by which rabies G disrupts neuronal function.

papers.title: Integrated Single Cell Analysis Reveals the Transcriptional Heterogeneity of Mouse Double Negative T Cells.
papers.abstract: Double negative T cells (DNT cells) are a rare T cell population involved in immune regulation, inflammation, autoimmunity, transplantation, and tumor immunity. However, their low abundance and dispersed distribution across tissues have limited a systematic understanding of their cellular organization and transcriptional diversity. To address this problem, we developed an integrative single cell framework to reconstruct the mouse DNT cell landscape across tissues using multiple public single cell RNA sequencing datasets. Using transcriptomic criteria, we identified and integrated 7984 mouse RN
papers.summary: This study develops an integrative single-cell framework to reconstruct the landscape of rare mouse double negative T cells (DNT cells) across tissues by combining multiple public scRNA-seq datasets, identifying 7,984 cells. The analysis reveals transcriptional heterogeneity within DNT cells, providing a systematic view of their cellular organization that was previously limited by their low abundance and dispersed distribution.

papers.title: Association mapping for canopy temperature under irrigated and rainfed conditions at 12 environments identified both known and novel genetic loci.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merrill) is the most widely cultivated oilseed crop and faces significant yield challenges due to drought stress. Canopy temperature has been proposed as an effective proxy for evaluation of differences in genotypic responses to water limitation, as well as indirectly assessing transpiration and stomatal conductance. Cooler canopy temperatures are associated with higher transpiration and open stomata, whereas warmer canopy temperatures are associated with reduced transpiration and stomatal closure. This study evaluated a diverse group of 205 soybean maturity group IV
papers.summary: This study performed association mapping in 205 diverse soybean genotypes across 12 environments to identify genetic loci linked to canopy temperature under irrigated and rainfed conditions. The analysis uncovered both previously known and novel loci, suggesting canopy temperature could serve as a useful proxy for drought tolerance breeding.

papers.title: From knowledge graph to topological data analysis: a novel framework to analyze gene regulatory networks for tomato-multi-pathogen interactions.
papers.abstract: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum), despite being the most important vegetable crop world-wide, remains vulnerable to over 200 diseases caused by different pests. Although tomato molecular response to individual stresses is well studied, the gene regulatory network (GRN) representing the crosstalk and trade-offs of multi-stress responses remains almost unexplored. We developed GENIAL (Gene rEgulatory Network and topologIcal datA anaLysis) to refine and analyze complex GRNs and TomTom, a knowledge graph that gathers 11 publicly available databases in a unique FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperabl
papers.summary: The authors developed GENIAL, a framework combining gene regulatory network (GRN) refinement with topological data analysis, and TomTom, a knowledge graph integrating 11 public databases, to study tomato responses to multiple pathogens simultaneously. This addresses a gap in understanding how tomato gene regulatory networks manage crosstalk and trade-offs during multi-stress conditions, which is largely unexplored compared to single-stress responses.

papers.title: iMPI: An Integrative Database for MicroProteins Encoded by Intron Retention in Tumors.
papers.abstract: Research advancements made in the last decade have shed light on the dysregulation of cellular mechanisms that lead to aberrant and pathologic intron retention (IR). IR is not merely a mechanism of gene regulation but may also play a potential role in cancer pathogenesis and therapeutic resistance across various human cancers. Despite its potential significance, there remains a notable gap in comprehensive database resources for introns within tumors. Therefore, we investigated whether the retained introns contain undiscovered protein-coding ORFs and whether they can encode proteins. We conduc
papers.summary: The authors built iMPI, a database cataloging microproteins that could be produced from retained introns in tumor transcriptomes, addressing a gap in resources linking intron retention to potential protein products. By systematically scanning retained introns for open reading frames, the work suggests that aberrant intron retention in cancer may generate previously unrecognized microproteins relevant to tumor biology.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Model-Informed Drug Development: Augmentation, Acceleration, and Regulatory Preparation.
papers.abstract: The convergence of MIDD and AI represents a natural evolution from established quantitative frameworks toward a broader, more powerful computational toolbox that can address persistent MIDD challenges such as high-dimensional data integration, complex biology, and operational constraints in evidence generation. AI can both enhance traditional MIDD through hybrid approaches and extend MIDD's horizon to include various AI models. Recent publications of guidance demonstrate the agency's preparation on the acceptance of AI in MIDD.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how artificial intelligence is being integrated into model-informed drug development (MIDD), both by enhancing existing quantitative frameworks and by enabling new AI-based models. It highlights that regulatory agencies are preparing guidance to accept AI in MIDD, signaling a shift toward broader computational approaches in drug development.

papers.title: Multimodality, interaction modeling, and multimodule architectures in genomic prediction: A unified conceptual framework.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of genomic, environmental, phenomic, and other high-dimensional data sources has transformed genomic prediction in plant breeding. However, the terms multimodal, interaction modeling, and multimodule architecture are often used inconsistently, generating ambiguity regarding whether they refer to biological assumptions, data integration strategies, or computational design. These dimensions are conceptually independent in the sense that none logically requires or implies the others. Interaction modeling may be implemented within a multimodule architecture, but modular computa
papers.summary: This paper proposes a unified conceptual framework to clarify the often-conflated terms 'multimodality,' 'interaction modeling,' and 'multimodule architectures' in genomic prediction for plant breeding. It argues these dimensions are conceptually independent—referring respectively to data integration strategies, biological assumptions, and computational design—and that conflating them creates ambiguity. The framework aims to help researchers and breeders more precisely describe and design prediction models that leverage diverse high-dimensional data sources.

papers.title: Mapping ovarian cellular and molecular landscape across the lifespan of women: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: With growing interest in ART, fertility preservation, and postmenopausal health of women, reproductive medicine is increasingly focused on characterizing oocytes and ovarian tissue composition, as well as understanding the molecular mechanisms that guide ovarian function throughout its lifecycle. High-throughput omics technologies have enabled the characterization of different molecular layers, leading to substantial advances in our understanding of their complex dynamics. However, not all molecular aspects are studied equally, and studies examining the same modalities often show inconsistenci
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes high-throughput omics studies of the human ovary across the female lifespan, covering oocytes and ovarian tissue composition. It highlights that molecular layers are studied unevenly and that findings across studies of the same modality are often inconsistent, pointing to gaps and methodological heterogeneity in reproductive omics.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence in animal genomics for smart agriculture: Applications, challenges, and future prospects.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a groundbreaking paradigm in the field of animal genomics and is providing the possibility to take a step towards intelligent agriculture, with better data integration, predictive modeling, and biological design. This review focuses on the shift from predictive to generative modelling paradigms, examining their implications for data synthesis, biological sequence design, and integrative smart livestock systems. It provides a comprehensive overview of recent developments, applications, and challenges at the intersection of generative AI and an
papers.summary: This review examines how generative AI is being applied to animal genomics for smart agriculture, focusing on the shift from predictive to generative modeling. It surveys applications in data synthesis, biological sequence design, and integrative livestock systems, while outlining challenges and future prospects.

papers.title: Re-emerging Marburg virus disease in Africa: spillover ecology, geographic expansion, and surveillance vulnerabilities.
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is re-emerging across Africa as a high-consequence zoonosis shaped by expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillover, and uneven surveillance capacity. This review synthesizes current evidence on the ecological, epidemiological, and operational determinants of contemporary Marburg virus (MARV) emergence. We conceptualize MVD as an ecological-emergence system produced by interactions among reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility, rather than as a series of isolated outbreaks. Recent detections in multi
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the re-emergence of Marburg virus disease across Africa, framing outbreaks as an ecological-emergence system driven by reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility. It highlights expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillovers, and uneven surveillance capacity as key determinants of contemporary MARV emergence.

papers.title: Comparative proteomic characterization of seminal plasma and sperm proteins associated with reproductive function in the Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus).
papers.abstract: Proteomic characterization of semen provides molecular insights into reproductive function beyond conventional semen evaluation. Although the seminal plasma and sperm proteomes of the common bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) have been reported, corresponding information for the Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus) is lacking. This study aimed to characterize the protein composition of seminal plasma and sperm in T. aduncus to identify proteins and biological pathways associated with reproductive function.
papers.summary: This study provides the first proteomic characterization of seminal plasma and sperm proteins in the Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus), a species for which such data were previously unavailable. The authors identify proteins and biological pathways linked to reproductive function, offering molecular insights that go beyond conventional semen evaluation. The work extends comparative proteomic knowledge from the common bottlenose dolphin to a closely related species.

papers.title: Beyond the autonomous individual: hydrosocial relations and the constitution of the relational hydrosocial self in an Andean conflict.
papers.abstract: This article addresses a specific under-theorized problem in social theory: how subjectivity is constituted through relations in which ecological and nonhuman entities are not contextual but constitutive. Against dominant models that define the self as autonomous, bounded, and human-centered, it argues that subject formation can emerge through hydrosocial relations linking humans, water systems, territory, and nonhuman entities. Drawing on qualitative fieldwork in the Razuhuillca micro-watershed in the Peruvian Andes, the study combines in-depth interviews, walking ethnography, field observati
papers.summary: This paper argues that human subjectivity is not solely an autonomous, human-centered phenomenon but can be constituted through relationships with water systems, territory, and nonhuman entities. Drawing on qualitative fieldwork in the Peruvian Andes, it develops the concept of the 'relational hydrosocial self' to describe how people's sense of self emerges from hydrosocial relations in a context of conflict.

papers.title: Grand challenge in microbiome data science: recovering the microbiome as a system.
papers.summary: This perspective piece frames the recovery of the microbiome as a coherent, interacting system—rather than a collection of independent taxa—as a grand challenge for microbiome data science. It argues that current analytical approaches often fail to capture ecological interactions, dynamics, and context-dependence, and calls for new computational frameworks that integrate multi-omics, network inference, and systems-level modeling. The paper is a conceptual roadmap rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and sports genomics: advancing precision sports science and athletic performance.
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and genomics in sports science has immense potential in the field by enabling personalised, predictive, and data-driven approaches to enhance athletes' performance and mitigate injury risk. Traditional training models based on generalised protocols may overlook individual variations in training adaptation, recovery, and injury susceptibility. Recent breakthroughs in genomics, wearable technologies, multi-omics profiling, and machine learning have produced new possibilities for precision sports medicine. This review explores the molecular and phys
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining artificial intelligence with sports genomics could enable personalized, predictive approaches to athletic training and injury prevention. It argues that traditional generalized training protocols fail to account for individual genetic and physiological variation, and that multi-omics profiling plus machine learning can support precision sports medicine.
